limits: Needs the network; a source that is down is reported beside the others' hits.
bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Relays the remote service's own result unchanged; it computes no number of its own, so the service is the authority for what comes back.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which archive records match this text?

description: Search the sequence archives by free text (a gene name, a protein, an organism, a phrase) across NCBI Nucleotide and Protein, ENA (plain records, WGS and TSA/TLS assembly sets, and annotated coding/non-coding features), UniProtKB and the iGEM Registry at once, and hand back the matching accessions. This is the half of Fetch from database that answers "which record do I want?"; fetch_record answers "give me that one". A source that is down does not fail the search: its error comes back beside the hits the others returned.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

limit.description: how many hits to ask each source for. The panel pages at this size, and every source is asked for the same number.

query.description: the words to search for. Archive query syntax is accepted where the archive accepts it, but plain words are the normal case: "beta-lactamase Escherichia coli", "GFP", "pUC19".

sources.description: which archives to ask. Each is searched independently and the hits are interleaved, so asking more costs time rather than accuracy. Defaults to the nucleotide pair the panel opens on.

name: search_records

accession.description: the top hit's accession, ready for a fetch_record node's $accession. This is the seam between searching and fetching

accessions.description: every hit’s accession, newline-separated, in the order they are ranked

hitCount.description: how many records came back across every source asked

hits.description: the full result rows: accession, title, source, organism, length, molecule kind and the archive’s own reported fields

source.description: which archive the top hit came from, ready for the same node's $source where the two vocabularies agree

unavailable.description: the sources that could not answer, each with the reason: empty when every source answered. A search is not a failure because one archive is down, and hiding that would make a short list read as a small literature
